chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made a bequest, saying: Abu Nayzar, Rabah, and Jubayr are to be emancipated on the condition that they work in the estate for five years.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: Made a bequest/testamentary disposition; a legally binding will
key_terms.الْمَالِ: Property/estate; in this context, the agricultural holdings managed by the slaves
key_terms.خَمْسَ سِنِينَ: Five years; the duration of the conditional service obligation
key_terms.عَتَقُوا: Emancipation/manumission; freedom from slavery granted legally

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about conditional emancipation of slaves in his bequest?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding a bequest made by Imam Ali (AS). The Commander of the Faithful stipulated that three of his slaves — Abu Nayzar, Rabah, and Jubayr — would be granted emancipation contingent on their continuing to work in the estate for five years. This reflects the jurisprudential concept of conditional manumission (al-'itq al-mu'allaq), which was recognized in Shia fiqh as binding, and establishes Imam Ali's practice of phased emancipation tied to continued service.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, or said Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdul Rahman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Abu Neyzara, and Rabaha, and Jubeyr
would be emancipated upon (a stipulation) that they work in the treasury for five years’.
